generation_notes: Revised to exactly 18 structurally valid candidate seed sequences grounded only in supplied IEC61850 sources. The library prioritizes framed MMS-over-ISO-on-TCP entries using documented TPKT+COTP+ACSE/UserInformation layering concepts, MMS PDU tags, confirmed service tags, GOOSE EtherType 0x88b8 with APDU outer tag 0x61 and field tags, and Sampled Values EtherType 0x88ba with APDU outer tag 0x60. Weak standalone crash-adjacent value blobs were replaced or upgraded into framed or APDU-structured analogues where possible. Evidence ids were cleaned to use only source chunk ids present in the supplied corpus. All BER lengths, outer TPKT lengths, and exact-size Ethernet relations were repaired to be self-consistent. Issue guidance was retained only as structural bias toward safe OCTET STRING, BIT STRING, count-bearing, ACSE, and size-sensitive shapes, while avoiding any exact collision with known payload bytes such as issue 193.

sequences.title: Canonical valid GetNameList over framed MMS transport
sequences.purpose: Provide a compact framed confirmed request using documented MMS Confirmed-Request-PDU and confirmed service tag [1] GetNameList with consistent TPKT and BER nesting.
sequences.expected_behavior: A receiver should accept TPKT and COTP CR framing, parse an AARQ-like ACSE wrapper, reach user-information, and then dispatch the embedded MMS Confirmed-Request-PDU to the GetNameList service path.
constraints_preserved: TPKT version is 0x03 and total length 0x0027 matches 39 bytes.
COTP CR length byte 0x11 matches the 17 bytes following it before ACSE content.
ACSE message type uses documented 0x60 AARQ.
ACSE context identifier is encoded as 02 01 01.
User-information tag 0xbe uses definite BER length.
Embedded MMS PDU tag is 0xa0 and confirmed service tag is [1] encoded as 0xa1.
All BER and transport lengths are self-consistent.
sequences.issue_safety_notes: This does not reproduce any known crash payload and avoids malformed or oversized lengths. It is a conservative framed request seed.

sequences.title: Stateful association then Initiate-Request-PDU
sequences.purpose: Provide a realistic small stateful sequence with client association setup, server association response, and a final initiate request to seed deeper state-dependent parser behavior.
sequences.expected_behavior: A test target should parse the setup AARQ, tolerate the compact AARE response, and then accept the final framed Initiate-Request-PDU for distinct stateful parser coverage.
constraints_preserved: Each message has a complete TPKT header with self-consistent total length.
Message 0 uses ACSE message type 0x60 AARQ and message 1 uses 0x61 AARE.
Message 2 uses documented MMS PDU tag 0xa8 for Initiate-Request-PDU.
COTP data TPDU 02f080 is used on data-bearing messages 1 and 2.
BER definite lengths are consistent in all three messages.
No negative lengths, truncation, or raw crash fragments are used.
sequences.issue_safety_notes: The sequence is issue-informed only in preferring valid state transitions over malformed setup. It is not an exact replay of any historical input.

sequences.title: GOOSE exact-size frame with tagged APDU fields
sequences.purpose: Provide a complete GOOSE Ethernet frame preserving the documented exact-size relation while also including realistic APDU field tags for better semantic coverage.
sequences.expected_behavior: A GOOSE parser should classify the frame by EtherType 0x88b8, observe the exact size relation, and then process the outer APDU tag 0x61 with multiple documented field tags including allData.
constraints_preserved: EtherType 0x88b8 is preserved.
GOOSE length field is 0x0061 and total frame length is exactly 14 plus 97 bytes.
GOOSE APDU outer tag is documented 0x61.
Included field tags are documented: 0x80 gocbRef, 0x85 stNum, 0x86 sqNum, 0x88 confRev, 0x8a numDatSetEntries, 0xab allData.
All BER lengths are internally consistent and no trailing padding is added.
sequences.issue_safety_notes: This keeps the issue-guided exact-size acceptance relation but replaces filler-only content with a safer tagged APDU and does not reuse any known PoC bytes.

sequences.title: Boundary-valid GetVariableAccessAttributes with long-form BER length

constraints_preserved: Outer MMS PDU tag is 0xa0 Confirmed-Request-PDU.
Outer length uses valid BER long-form encoding 81 10 for 16 bytes of content.

Inner visible string length matches the supplied content bytes.
All lengths are internally consistent.
sequences.issue_safety_notes: This seed avoids malformed or oversized boundary lengths and instead uses a valid long-form BER encoding suitable for safe mutation.

global_feedback: The library has good breadth across MMS, ACSE-wrapped transport, GOOSE, and SAV, and it usefully attempts issue-guided analogues without directly copying known crash payloads.
The strongest seeds are the fully framed transport entries and the Ethernet GOOSE/SAV frames, because they are most likely to survive early parser checks and reach deeper code.
Several standalone MMS BER seeds are too speculative: many use service bodies or nested tags that are not grounded by the supplied IEC61850/MMS templates, so claimed validity is not well supported.
A number of seeds claim strict length self-consistency, but multiple hex blobs have mismatched BER lengths or questionable tag/body combinations; this materially lowers protocol confidence.
The stateful sequence is directionally useful, but its AARQ/AARE content is minimal and partly inconsistent with the claimed operations; it should be tightened if retained as a premium seed.

Issue enhancement is mostly handled appropriately: structures are inspired by sensitive surfaces while avoiding direct PoC replay, but some analogues are so generic that they may not map to realistic parser states.

For a desired final selected seed count of 12, the current set should be pruned to the best-framed and most defensible candidates and several speculative standalone MMS blobs should be revised or dropped.

IEC 61850 Function and Service Code Reference
=============================================

Important Note
--------------
IEC 61850 does not define one single "Function Code" field like Modbus.

IEC 61850 operations are represented through:

1. MMS PDU types
2. MMS confirmed service tags
3. MMS unconfirmed service tags
4. IEC 61850 ACSI service names
5. GOOSE EtherType and APDU fields
6. Sampled Values EtherType and APDU fields
7. Control model values

For an IEC 61850 function-code corpus, the MMS service tag is the closest
equivalent to a Modbus function code.

================================================================
1. IEC 61850 TRANSPORT AND PROTOCOL IDENTIFIERS
================================================================

TCP Port:

102 = MMS over ISO-on-TCP

EtherType:

0x88B8 = GOOSE
0x88BA = Sampled Values
0x88F7 = Precision Time Protocol

OSI transport commonly used for MMS:

TPKT
COTP
ACSE
Presentation
MMS

================================================================
2. MMS PDU TYPE TAGS
================================================================

0xA0 = Confirmed-Request-PDU
0xA1 = Confirmed-Response-PDU
0xA2 = Confirmed-Error-PDU
0xA3 = Unconfirmed-PDU
0xA4 = Reject-PDU
0xA5 = Cancel-Request-PDU
0xA6 = Cancel-Response-PDU
0xA7 = Cancel-Error-PDU
0xA8 = Initiate-Request-PDU
0xA9 = Initiate-Response-PDU
0xAA = Initiate-Error-PDU
0xAB = Conclude-Request-PDU
0xAC = Conclude-Response-PDU
0xAD = Conclude-Error-PDU

================================================================
3. MMS CONFIRMED SERVICE TAGS
================================================================

Issue: 516
Summary: A fuzzing-discovered out-of-bounds write was reported in libiec61850 in `BerEncoder_encodeBitString` in `src/mms/asn1/ber_encoder.c`. The issue is triggered while encoding `MMS_BIT_STRING` `MmsData`: the function writes the tag, encoded length, padding byte, and bit-string bytes into `buffer` by advancing `bufPos`, but the report says it does not properly validate that `bufPos` stays within the valid buffer range. The report states this can occur if `bitStringSize` is large enough or if `bufPos` is already near the end of the buffer, resulting in writes past the end of `buffer`.
Reproduce: No build flags or commands are provided in the report. The provided PoC is a fuzz-style harness linked against libiec61850 and using `iec61850_server.h`, `hal_thread.h`, and `lib_memory.h`. To reproduce, create `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput(const char *data, size_t size)` that: (1) calls `MmsValue_decodeMmsData(data, 0, size, &out)`; (2) returns if decoding fails; (3) calls `MmsValue_encodeMmsData(mmsValue, NULL, 0, false)` to get `dataSize`; (4) allocates `dataSize` bytes with `GLOBAL_MALLOC`; (5) calls `MmsValue_encodeMmsData(mmsValue, mmsBuffer, 0, true)` to re-encode the value; and then (6) frees the buffer and deletes the `MmsValue`. Feed the harness the byte sequence provided in the report, beginning `"<84><81><80><00><30><30>..."` and continuing with repeated `<30>` bytes exactly as listed there. The report states that this input reaches `BerEncoder_encodeBitString` while encoding `MMS_BIT_STRING` data and triggers an out-of-bounds write. No specific crash log or sanitizer output is included.

global_feedback: The library shows good breadth across MMS PDU tags, GOOSE, and SAV, and it generally avoids direct replay of known crash payloads.
The strongest seeds are the few that use complete transport framing and internally consistent lengths, especially the canonical confirmed-request seeds and the GOOSE exact-size analogue.

A major weakness is overclaiming protocol validity for many standalone BER blobs and minimal PDUs whose inner MMS semantics are not supported by the supplied sources; these are weak as initial seeds for a network parser unless the harness truly consumes isolated MMS TLVs.

Several seeds target response, reject, or error PDUs as standalone inputs without the surrounding association state that would usually make them meaningful; these are lower-value than valid client request flows.

The stateful sequence is directionally correct and useful, but the setup request uses service tag [2] while labeling it as Identify-like only indirectly, and the final Initiate-Request-PDU is extremely skeletal.

Issue enhancement is only partially convincing: the analogues are structurally safer and not copied from crash payloads, but many are too generic and insufficiently grounded in documented IEC 61850/MMS framing to be strong corpus starters.
The deterministic validator removed many unknown evidence ids, which does not directly invalidate payloads but suggests weak grounding and should be cleaned up.
For a desired final selected seed count of 12, keep the best framed and most coverage-useful seeds, and revise or drop the weakest standalone minimal PDUs.

global_feedback: The library has good breadth across MMS, ACSE-wrapped transport, GOOSE, and SAV, and it usefully attempts issue-guided analogues without directly copying known crash payloads.
The strongest seeds are the fully framed transport entries and the Ethernet GOOSE/SAV frames, because they are most likely to survive early parser checks and reach deeper code.
Several standalone MMS BER seeds are too speculative: many use service bodies or nested tags that are not grounded by the supplied IEC61850/MMS templates, so claimed validity is not well supported.
A number of seeds claim strict length self-consistency, but multiple hex blobs have mismatched BER lengths or questionable tag/body combinations; this materially lowers protocol confidence.
The stateful sequence is directionally useful, but its AARQ/AARE content is minimal and partly inconsistent with the claimed operations; it should be tightened if retained as a premium seed.

Issue enhancement is mostly handled appropriately: structures are inspired by sensitive surfaces while avoiding direct PoC replay, but some analogues are so generic that they may not map to realistic parser states.

For a desired final selected seed count of 12, the current set should be pruned to the best-framed and most defensible candidates and several speculative standalone MMS blobs should be revised or dropped.
